Sand and Padina macro-algae in the grooves. Fsih depauperate - few species few numbers, and larger species absent.

Coral mortality looks old – maybe a combination of southern facing reef edge so very exposed in SE trade winds, possibly cyclone damage and a large bleaching event – perhaps 1998?

Reef plateau at 5m with dead coral and sand and in areas very high live coral - some large areas of live Pavona and encrusting Montipora, and live Acropora plates (over 2m in diameter) at 6m. Reef edge at 5m drops 70-90 degrees and at ~ 14m to 17m live coral cover high – large areas of Montipora, large Acropora plates. Huge colony of Pavona. Many fungids. Reef extends out in a spur before turning into the channel. Here bottom of sand can be seen at ~ 17m. No sign of any damage from fishing gears. Another “coral garden”! Fish relatively abundant at this site, and larger – L. harak, Monotaxis grandoculis, some L. bohar, larger parrotfishes. But no grouper.

Sandy plateau with isolated coral patches at ~ 6m. Then slopes at 45-65 degrees to a sand bottom at ~ 25m. Forereef with moderate live coral cover, and realtively diverse in places, and high cover of Echinopora in other areas. On steeper slopes coral ends at 12m and then a slope of rubble and sand to ~ 17m. Bubble coral (Plerogyra or Physogyra) common. Halimeda present. Damaged and broken coral in places with soft corals common. Dead coral looks like fishing gear damage, maybe ringnet gear or even dynamite. Fish density and diversity low.

Narrow strip of small patches of reef on inner side of Fundo Island at 3-6 m, bordering patches of seagrass and large areas of sand. Turbid. Some live coral, notably Lobophyllia, Galaxea and Platygyra. Sea whips. Halimeda in places at 6m. Soft corals and sponges dominate, with dead coral and some rubble. Some sea urchins. Several juvenile scarids, labrids relativel diverse,

Narrow strip of reef on inner side of Fundo Island further north of FGI_01, slightly more structure and corals at 4-8 m, bordering patches of seagrass and large areas of sand. Seagrass also seaward of the reef strip. A lot of old dead coral, many sponges including very large vase sponges, hydroids, anemones. Mulloidichthys flavolineatus common.

Forereef of 70 degree wall, drops out of sight beyond 20m. Mostly dead coral, some very small Porites colonies are some of the only live coral. Lots of sand, very similar to FUO_01. Cold upwelling. Lots of planktivores – Naso spp, especially N. thynnoides.

Sand plateau at 5m with scattered dead coral and sponges, some massive Porites and many sea urchins. Reef edge at 10-11m and then drops at 90 degrees to sand and dead coral. Some large dead corals have fallen down the steep wall. Sponges abundant from 9m down. Small Porites bommies relatively common. Forereef of mainly high rugosity dead coral, sand and rubble, with very large pieces of broken coral. Looks like some sort of destructive fishing perhaps – maybe ringnetting? Not fully clear why the reef is so dead  - to beyond visibility, could not see the bottom.Relatively abundant fish compared to other sites and moderately diverse. First schools of snapper – Lutjanus kasmira, lots of fusiliers and Lethrinus harak, and parrotfish more abundant here compared to other sites, with some of the first TPs seen – eg Scarus russelli. Cephalopholis miniata also quite common and relatively large
Reef comprises, dead coral, sand, rock and algal turf, some macro-algae. No soft coral. Aphareus furca and Pterois sp. relatively common.

Spur and groove structure reef close to shore with low relief and some silt, dominated by rubble and soft coral, with sand and rubbles in the grooves. Live coral ~ 20% dominated by small Porites heads. Anemones quite common. Top plateau at ~ 10m then drops steeply to rubble. Rubbish common especially nappies!
Basaltic slope, makes a plateau at 20ºfrom 5m to 15m depth with lots of small porites and scattered large rocky relief, then drops with 50º. Fewer acropora, high soft coral cover

Steep slope and wall dropping to 40m+.  High hard coral cover >85% with lot of leafy hard corals. Low fish abundance

Inner protected reef in Chole Bay. Complex topography (rugosity 4) with pinnacles with steep walls covered with sponges and ascidians, and elsewhere soft corals and brown algae common, live hard coral relatively uncommon.
Shallow lagoonal reef plateau at 5-3m. Short slope to 8m with Galaxea, branching Acropora going to algae and sand bottom. Very high live coral cover.

Forereef slope at 35 degrees to rubble and sand bottom at 18-20m. Slope dominated by soft corals, sponges, some live corals including plate Acropora (two very large plates). Some very large boulders and overhangs
Scattered boulders on sand and rubble on slope of 20 degrees to 13m, dominated by macro algae, mainly Lobophora, Milipora also abundant, and dead coral and hydroids.
Reef plateau at 4-2m. High live coral cover. Coral and sand patch slope to 10-15m. Some patches of soft corals and dead hard corals.

Thin strip of scattered coral bommies on sand / rock base off wider sand flat in centre of Kokota island facing centre of channel between Kukota and Uvinje. Dominated by large vase sponges, some small black Tubastrea, soft corals very common. Low topography and large expanses of sand. Low fish density and diversity.

In the channel site is towards northern end of Kukota island. Several live coral heads – Acropora, Favites, Pocillopora, in 2- 3m on sand very close to coral cliff of Kukota island. Reef edge at 4m and drops steeply at 80 degrees. High cover of live encrusting corals on wall, many hydroids, many unidentified small very thin spiky white coral (not hermatypic). Sea whips common. Undulating reef slope with large banks of Echinopora in the more gently sloping grooves. Walls carpeted with high cover and diversity of largely encrusting and small massive corals to ~17m. Sponges common. Reef ends at around 25m in channel of sand. Turbid, viz at 9m. Cold water at > 11m. Small acanthurid species,  pomacentrids and tobies common. Moderate diversity of small labrid species.

Seagrass on the landward shallow at 7-8m. Hard corals and soft corals  at 11m on flat reef then dominated by macroalgae from 13m with isolated hard coral colonies at 15m. Macroalgae and sand pacthes from 18m  montipora.

Sand and scattered coral heads at 3- 4m, with some Diadema. Reef edge at ~ 5m, with forereef wall sloping 70-90 degrees with overhangs and ledges, very little live coral > 17m depth. Reef wall gives way to sand at ~ 20-25 m which slopes at 40 degrees beyond visibility. At 13-16m a zone of relatively high coral cover, mainly encrusting low topography forms, several genera, and also soft corals. Depleted  numbers, but some small schools of Lethrinus harak. Some very large Cheilinus trilobatus males. This species and Hologymnus species (fascistus and doliatus) relatively common compared to elsewhere. More parrotfishes but all small – including Chlorurus strongylocephalos. Chaetodons common and diverse

Reef plateau at 6-7m of sand, dead coral and many soft corals. Reef edge at 7m which then slopes at ~ 50 degrees to 16m, then 70 degrees to ~ 20m. This forereef comprises ledges, sand and rock with sponges and some live coral. High dead coral at ~ 15m with sponges abundant. Beyond 20m a 50 degree slope of largely sand and sponges disappearing into depths. Shallow areas are very dead and broken up – a mix of very old bleaching mortality and possibly ring net damage – coral pieces are large and loose suggesting some physical disturbance. Fish depleted. Lethrinus harak relatively abundant. Afew scarids but very low numbers and all small.
Reef flat at ~ 3 m with several small coral heads, largely Acropora on old rubble and several large urchins (Echinometra mathae?). Wall of Galaxea at ~  7m – 10m at 60 degrees to sand bottom.

Shallow plateau at 1-2 m, short slope at ~4m to ~10m, ends on sand. Shallow plateau is largely dead reef of Acropora staghorn and plates, some live Acropora and small Pocillopora, large areas of sand.
30 degree slope of sand with scattered dead coral and algae, Lobophora dominate and some Halimeda. Reef ends at 12-15m to gentle sand and rubble slope. Less than 10, almost entirely algae.
Rock and algae reef on sand, very dead. Occasional live Porites, other small massives, dead standing large Acropora plates, one live plate sighted. Turbinaria and brown algae Lobophora.

Deep narrow spur and groove structure with grooves of sand, close to rocky cliff shore. Sand bottom at 15m with scattered high bommies. Moderately high dead coral, silt and rubble. Top of spurs with higher coral cover, mostly Acropora. Dead coral looks like old die off from bleaching. fish not very diverse and densities fairly low, several snapper species.

Spur and groove structured reef to sand at around 20m. Largely dead coral on the shallow part of the plateau before the edge, looks like old bleaching damage, rock now covered in turf algae with some silt.. Somw coral re-growth and CCA high. Favids quite common, black coral at 16m. Diversity moderately high, eg Coris aygula. Some very large schools of Lutjanus gibbus, large schools of Kyphosus sp. and moderately large schools of Gymnocranius grandoculis.

Large dead Acropora plates at ~ 7m bordering sand. Reef edge not distinct – rolling ridges of coral and grooves of sand until hard reef edge at 14-15m which then slopes at 50 degrees to sand at ~ 20m. Live coral cover high from around 14m. Many encrusting species – Echinopora etc. The shallow reef ~ 6m dominated by soft corals, dead corals, sponges. Fish populations depleted.

Spectacular forereef with very high live coral cover from reef edge at 13m, but with some small areas of sand and rubble. Wall from ~ 16m at 85 degrees and at around 20m coral presence declines, and continues beyond visibility. Some bleached and dead coral particularly Acropora and on reef plateau at 6 – 9m very high mortality of large Acropora plates. Likely from bleaching and looks old – prior to 2016.Fish very depleted. Scarids present and fairly high species diversity but numbers very low. Chaetodon diversity high. 3 Cephalopholis argus but no other groupers. Fishing line very common

Less distinct spur and groove structure and quite silty, but good coral cover - ~50%. Reef drops to sand, small rocks with turf-algae and silt with scattered mushroom corals (Fungia) at 20-25m. Some coral mortality eg of large Acropora plates. Subragorgia at 22m. Encrusting Goniopora notable and large domes of Favia. Several brain corals, some large Porites bommies in shallows – around 8m. Reef is subtidal flat much closer to shore. Very reduced fish numbers and species. BUt 1 Epineph. flavocaeruleus and Plec laevis. 
1 Plectropomus laevis and 1 Epinehphelus flavocaeruleus.

Shallow forereef fringing mainland which ends on sand at between 10m and 15m. Very rugose with some large Porites, diverse corals, but only about 30% live coral, and also lots of soft coral and turf algae particularly on shallow plateau which is largely dead with turf and several Acanthurus lineatus. Silty.  Fish numbers  and species low. 1 Epinephelus flavocaeruleus.

Broken up reef edge, lots of dead coral wth turf algae. Some rubble and large boulders with turf. Lots of silt. Large sand patches. Looks like coral mortality from old bleaching event, and possibly some dynamite fishing since rubble and coral boulders are large. Slope ends on sand at ~20m. Live coral largely Pocillopora and Porites. 1 Epinephelus multinotatus.

Forereef with spur and groove structure slopes steeply and quickly to sand bottom with isolated bommies at ~ 15m. High live coral (~50%) on reef edge favids, Acropora, Goniopora, areas of staghorn Acropora in shallows (~6m). Some silt, large areas of sand. Moderate rogusity. Few fish, but parrotfish diversity relatively high, though numbers low. Three large Cetoscarus ocellatus males, Sphyraena barracuda.
Extensive HC and SC from shallow 2m to about 8m . Filamentous algae + lobophyta MA, flat sandy substrate after 8m

Reef on a slope of 20 ending at 10m. Rich hard corals and soft corals with massive posites and asteopora. Seagrass and sand from 10m

Outer fringing reef. Flat at 5m, macroalgea, rock & sand dominated. 20 degree slope to sand and macroalgea at 10. Very few live corals, very occasional small porties bommies. Transects done on the landward side of the slope.

Beautiful complex reef with rich coral growth and diversity but few fish. Spur and groove structure ~500 metres from shore. Gentle slope and then drops at ~ 17m steeply at 65 degrees where encrusting Goniopora dominates. Saw Subragonia octocoral at ~ 25m but was too shallow to return to photograph it. But few fish.
Steeply sloping reef at 13-15m with encrusting Porites and others eg. Pachyseris? Very high coral cover ~ 70% on spurs. Several large Chlor strongylocephalos & Monotaxis grandoculis.

Rich coral growth, moderately high diversity, some large favids, some large plates, ~ 70% cover, moderately high rugosity. Fringing islet facing south and slopes fairly steeply at ~ 45 degrees to sand and rubble at ~ 20-25m. Parrotifsh quite common and diverse and TP present and quite large. 1 Plectropomus laevis.

Reef fringes rock wall of island with a shallow plateau at ~ 5m, which then drops at ~45 degrees with very rich coral growth, to around 20m of sand and rubble. Corals dominated by various Acropora, domes of Favia and large stands of digitate Porites. Moderate fish diversity; several parrotfish, some very large, such as Scarus rubroviolaceus. Some large Plectropomus laevis –one strange mottled colour, not seen before, and Variola louti common.

Fringing reef with spur and groove structure, sloping to rubble, sand and silt at ~ 20m. High cover of live coral, encrusting Goniopora notable,  but also areas of rubbles and silt; slightly turbid, and some macro-algae. Fish diversity quite high.

Wide shelf of reef with spur and groove structure. High coral growth on spurs but mostly rubble in the grooves. Corals continue to at least 30m – slope covered with mainly encrusting plate corals at >20m. Highly varied topography – high rugosity. Several parrotfish and surgeon fish, notably several large Naso brachycentron and N. unicornis, though the latter two never in transects! Monotaxis grandoculis, large and several. An enormous Lutjanus bohar (>70cm), several Plectropomus laevis.

well develop reef slope 35 degrees with spurs. Moderate live coral mainly small heads. CCA high. Patches of soft and anenom and drop steeply over 80m to sand with ledges. Huge schools of 11cm L. kasmira and L. gibbus. School of 20 C. melampagus, 1 green turle, no big groupoers.E.melanostigma  - is correct, 1 melanostigma recorded but no photo so cannot verify, but definately not spilotoceps.

Small patches of hard coral on flat dominated by macroalgea, seagrass and sand

Gentle slope of sand at 20 degrees with scattered coral patches, some live, especially massive corals, soft corals and sponges. Halimeda algae very common especially near the reef edge. Some dead corals and large Acroprora plates corals dead or partially dead, but structure intact, likely old bleaching. Massive corals live – Favia, Favites, Pleriogyra (?) etc.. Edge at 12m. Wall drops very steeply with ledges and large fans and sponges. Still on wall at 27m, and bottom not seen! No live coral observed on wall and very few fish, felt like a mesophotic reef! Strongly depleted, no groupers, no lutjanids, but scarids present.

Gentle slope of 15 degrees at reef top in 8-10m, with banks of live Echinopora and some Galaxea. Some patches of dead coral and areas of soft corals. Fish trap and a set bottom gillnet. Reef edge at ~ 12- 13m depth and then drops at 50 degrees to sand bottom at ~ 30m. Steep slope has almost full cover of hard coral – primarily extensive banks of Galaxea and Echinopora. Several other corals also present – fungids, Acropora, Pocillopora. Very healthy stretch of reef except for fish pop - strongly depleted, no groupers, only 3 individual emperors and no reef lutjanids, but chaetodons quite diverse and scarids are present.

Southside of reef pass / island channel. Fairly strong current, particularly at surface, going out to sea, this before high tide. Reef plateau at 7-10m dominated by Halimeda, moderately high topography of very large coral bommies, mostly dead. Slopes to reef edge at ~ 13m then a wall that drops at 90 degrees in the channel to a sand slope at around ~25m which slopes at ~ 70 degrees. Sand a common substrate. Wall has fans, and many sponges. Some small Acropora. Fish highly depleted. Kyphosids quite common on plateau. 12 giant barracuda.
Degraded reef at 10m with high ruef algae and halimeda, gentle slope ~20 to 10m then flat sand and rubble, some colonies of pachyseris and echinophyllia. Medium relief from DC

Flat inner shallow terrace. Large porites bommies, which are exposed at low tide, surrounded by sandy patches and macroalgea covered dead coral.
Very extensive reef plateau (2-8m) of dead stag horn Acropora, areas of dead plate Acropora; high cover of brown algae (large leaf), several small live coral heads, CCA common.
Patches of coral reefs end on sand at ~ 12m. Coral (Millepora) and black sponges very common. Live corals scattered but with large areas of Pachyseris and Lobophyllia.

Extremely damaged reef. Dead and broken up reef and sand plateau at ~ 5m. Looks exactly like dynamite damage – large scattered pieces of old coral. High level of rubble. Diadema urchins abundant. Sand dominates. Reef crest at ~ 12 m to sandy slope. Scattered dead coral pieces covered with soft corals, some sponges. Low topography. Occasional small live Acroprora and Porites. “Reef” ends on sand at ~ 25m, with bommies visible further offshore on sand. Very few fish. Several species of small labrids present

Galaxia abundant on reef top at 4m with diverse algae, Lobophora and Halimeda dominate. Slope to sand bottom at 10-12m. Areas of sand and rubble with red algae. Relative high and diverse live coral cover in patches

spurs on sand to around 15m depth then sand. Very scarce live hard coral (small Acropora) on the spurs. Fish depleted

Very dead broken up reef plateau at ~ 4m depth, no live coral, gives way to sand sloping at ~ 50 degrees. Large areas of rubble on the sand slope. No live coral or bommies on the slope. Diadema sea urchins very common. Fish highly depleted. No grouper species at all. Small labrid species relatively common.

Reef plateau at 5-10m of broken up dead coral – looks like old dynamite damage because coral structure does not resemble death from bleaching and collapse of finer structure. Coral structure is overturned and broken up. Could reflect severe cyclone but they don’t occur here. Soft corals abundant. Very few live hard corals. Plateau then slopes at 40 degrees, largely sand but with some coral outcrops at ~ 15m depth of moderately large colonies of live Pavona. Depleted fish populations, snappers notably absent, but small groupers (Cephalopholis spp) common.

Sand and largely dead reef flat at 4-5 m; slopes to edge at ~ 8m and then a sandy slope dropping at 50 degrees. Sea urchins abundant especially on reef flat. More live coral on sand slope, and the most seen so far on the survey. Nevertheless reef dominated by sand and rubble. Soft coral common on rock/dead coral. Depleted numbers and diversity of fish but schools of small Aprion viriscens.

Reef flat of rubble and sand. Edge at 8m, slope all dead, mainly rubble and sand and soft coral. Similar to SHI_01. Fish highly depleted. But Ctenochaetus species abundant. Some larger planktivorous Naso species off the reef edge.
Flat inner lagoon reef. Macroalgea and seagrass dominanted with dead hard coral patches.
Flat fringing reef at 10m, slope at 30 degrees to ~20m. Mostly macroalgea with some patches of soft corals

Forereef slope at 35 degrees to rubble and sand bottom at 18-20m. Slope dominated by soft corals, sponges and rock with sand patches. Several live corals, including plate Acropora, Pocillopora common and Porites

Wall slopes at ~ 75 degrees to around 22m, composed of bare rock covered in low turf like algae, brown and green, sand, occasional small hard corals. Appears to be more of an algal reef not coral reef. Upper plateau dominated by algea.
